raw_response:
I’m already old, so I won’t toss all 6 mu into one thing and gamble on the year. What has kept my family steady is to split the land: part in cotton for cash, part in wheat followed by summer maize so we still have grain and some insurance if cotton price or weather goes bad. I’ve farmed here a long time, and around Quzhou if wheat looks weak from lack of base fertilizer, you usually regret it later, so I still put a decent base dose. But I also can’t spend too much at once. Some people in the family work outside, so on the field side I want a plan that is steady, not too fancy, and can be managed with the labor we have at key times.

This year I’ll keep 3 mu in cotton and 3 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. Cotton gives cash, but it needs more watching for insects and more hand labor at picking, so I won’t expand it. For wheat I’ll do what I trust: sow on time in October, use a moderate seed rate, base fertilizer plus one topdress at jointing, and irrigate when the crop really needs it. Right after wheat harvest, I’ll rush in maize on the same 3 mu with simple tillage so I don’t miss soil moisture. I won’t chase the highest yield with heavy fertilizer because pumping water costs money and family labor is not always at home, but I also won’t cut inputs too hard because under-doing it is riskier for me than spending a little extra.
